On the 1980 sample it is `r sg(pw(PW8, "m13", "m12"))` (SE `r fmt(pw(PW8, "m13", "m12", "se_diff"), 1)` / `r fmt(pw(PW8, "m13", "m12", "se_diff_nw"), 1)`; z `r fmt(z138, 2)`). One quarter dominates the uncertainty. 2020 Q2 alone contributes `r sg(d1312f$d[d1312f$date == q2])` nats on the full sample and `r sg(d13128$d[d13128$date == q2])` on the 1980 sample: m12's constant latent variance cannot accommodate the collapse. Outside 2020 Q2 to 2021 Q1 the full-sample gain is `r sg(fv("m13", "m12", "all excl. COVID"))` (NW SE `r fmt(fv("m13", "m12", "all excl. COVID", "se_nw_full"), 1)`); before 2020 it is `r sg(fv("m13", "m12", "pre-2020"))` (z `r fmt(fv("m13", "m12", "pre-2020", "z_nw_full"), 1)`). m13 is ahead in `r sum(d1312f$d > 0)` of 146 quarters. Outside 2020 the gain per quarter grows over the window, as latent volatility falls further below m12's constant. On the 1980 sample the pre-2020 gain is only `r sg(fv("m13", "m12", "pre-2020", "diff_sample"))` (z `r fmt(fv("m13", "m12", "pre-2020", "z_nw_sample"), 2)`), and m13 is ahead in `r sum(d13128$d > 0)` quarters. Excluding all of 2020 to 2022, the gain is `r sg(sum(ex2022(d1312f)$d))` (z `r fmt(sum(ex2022(d1312f)$d) / nw(ex2022(d1312f)$d), 2)`) on the full sample and `r sg(sum(ex2022(d13128)$d))` (z `r fmt(sum(ex2022(d13128)$d) / nw(ex2022(d13128)$d), 2)`) on the 1980 sample.

m13 was proposed after the re-specified m10, which has latent SV, had been scored on the same window and had beaten m12 on the GDP-only target. m13 is therefore a second latent-SV specification evaluated on the same data. Counting only those two tries, a Bonferroni-adjusted two-sided 5% bar is z ≈ `r fmt(qnorm(1 - 0.05 / 4), 2)`, which `r fmt(z13f, 2)` does not meet. That bar is a lower bound on the correction: the old m10, the re-specified m10, m12 and m13 were all scored on the same 146 targets. The direction of the evidence is clear: latent volatility has changed a great deal over the sample (@fig-tau). Its strength as a test of predictive improvement is modest.

**The structural restriction is predictively neutral.** m9 − m4 is `r sg(pw(PWf, "m9", "m4"))` (z `r fmt(pw(PWf, "m9", "m4", "z_nw"), 2)`) on the full sample, and m6 − m2 is `r sg(pw(PWf, "m6", "m2"), 2)`. On the 1980 sample they are `r sg(pw(PW8, "m9", "m4"))` and `r sg(pw(PW8, "m6", "m2"), 2)`. m9 − m4 on the 1980 sample is within the particle-filter uncertainty of these models in 2020 Q2 (@sec-robust-pf) and falls to `r sg(rs(RS8, "m9", "m4", "first"), 2)` with first refit attempts only. We keep the restriction because it reflects how the measures are built, not because the data favour it.

**COVID variance scale.** m7 − m1 is `r sg(pw(PWf, "m7", "m1"))` (z `r fmt(pw(PWf, "m7", "m1", "z_nw"), 2)`) on the full sample. Its gain comes from 2020, and m7 knows in advance which quarters to scale. On the full sample m7's 2020 Q2 scale factor is `r pci("m7_full", "kappa[1]", 1)`, while the scale factors for the other three quarters have medians of `r fmt(pv("m7_full", "kappa[2]"), 2)`, `r fmt(pv("m7_full", "kappa[3]"), 2)` and `r fmt(pv("m7_full", "kappa[4]"), 2)`. m7 therefore treats essentially all of the 2020 Q2 collapse as measurement error: its latent growth in 2020 Q2 has posterior mean `r sg(cov("m7_full"))` on the full sample and `r sg(cov("m7_1980"))` on the 1980 sample, against a headline of `r fmt(hl_2020q2, 1)`. Its variance ratio, `r fmt(vr("m7_full", "1959Q4-2026Q2"), 2)`, is the lowest of the full-sample models.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sub
#| tbl-cap: "Score differences by sub-period (nats). Each cell gives the full-sample run / the 1980-sample run. 'Excl. COVID' drops 2020 Q2–2021 Q1. Newey-West SEs for the longer periods are in the text and in output/sample_1980/tables/lfo_full_vs_sample.csv."
prs <- list(c("m5", "m2"), c("m12", "m9"), c("m4", "m2"), c("m9", "m6"), c("m9", "m4"), c("m13", "m12"))
per <- c("1990-99", "2000-07", "2008-19", "2020", "2021-22", "2023-26", "pre-2020", "all excl. COVID", "all")
cellS <- function(a, b, p) {
  x <- paste0(fmt(fv(a, b, p, "diff_full"), 1), "/", fmt(fv(a, b, p, "diff_sample"), 1))
  x }
ts <- sapply(prs, function(p) sapply(per, cellS, a = p[1], b = p[2]))
ts <- data.frame(Period = c("1990–99", "2000–07", "2008–19", "2020", "2021–22", "2023–26", "pre-2020", "excl. COVID", "all 146"), ts, check.names = FALSE)
names(ts)[-1] <- sapply(prs, function(p) paste0(p[1], " − ", p[2]))
tab(ts, align = "lrrrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-cum
#| fig-cap: "Cumulative score differences over the 146 LFO targets (nats). Left: full-sample run (training from 1959 Q4). Right: 1980-sample run (training from 1980 Q1)."
cumd <- function(LP, a, b, s) { x <- pdiff(LP, a, b); data.frame(date = x$date, cum = cumsum(x$d), pair = paste(a, "−", b), s = s) }
cd <- rbind(do.call(rbind, lapply(prs[c(1, 2, 3, 6)], function(p) cumd(LPf, p[1], p[2], "Full sample"))),
            do.call(rbind, lapply(prs[c(1, 2, 3, 6)], function(p) cumd(LP8, p[1], p[2], "1980 sample"))))
cd$s <- factor(cd$s, levels = c("Full sample", "1980 sample"))
p5 <- ggplot(cd, aes(date, cum, colour = pair)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_step(linewidth = 0.5) + facet_wrap(~s) +
  scale_colour_manual(NULL, values = c("#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3", "#e7298a")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "cumulative Δ elpd (nats)") + theme_minimal(base_size = 9) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
f5 <- "figures/fig5_lfo_cumulative.png"
ggsave(f5, p5, width = 6.5, height = 3.3, dpi = 200)
knitr::include_graphics(f5)
```

@tbl-sub and @fig-cum show where the differences arise. The serial-correlation gain (m5 − m2) accumulates steadily, mostly in the 1990s and 2000s. The measurement-SV gain (m4 − m2) builds from 2000 and is largest in 2008–19 and 2023–26. It falls back in 2020 on the full sample. The latent-SV gain (m13 − m12) is small in the 1990s, grows through the 2010s and jumps in 2020 Q2. On the 1980 sample m12 is slightly ahead of m13 in 1990–99 (`r fmt(fv("m13", "m12", "1990-99", "diff_sample"), 1)`, NW z `r fmt(fv("m13", "m12", "1990-99", "z_nw_sample"), 2)`).

**Labour-market models.** On the hours subsample the re-specified m10 is ahead of m8, which has constant variances, by `r sg(pw(PWf, "m10", "m8", comp = G2))` nats on the joint four-signal target (z `r fmt(pw(PWf, "m10", "m8", "z_nw", G2), 2)`). This gain is post hoc in the sense above. On the GDP-only target, $\log p(y^{E,I,P}_t \mid y_{1:t-1})$ with hours in the past but not in the target, m13 is ahead of m10 by `r sg(pw(PWf, "m13", "m10", comp = GO))` (z `r fmt(pw(PWf, "m13", "m10", "z_nw", GO), 2)`) and of the mixed-frequency m11 by `r sg(pw(PWf, "m13", "m11", comp = GO))` (z `r fmt(pw(PWf, "m13", "m11", "z_nw", GO), 2)`). These gaps do not measure the value of labour data. m10 has neither AR(1) errors nor the E–I correlation, m11 has no SV, and no m13-plus-hours model was fitted. m11 also conditions on employment inside the target quarter, which is released before GDP.

# Robustness {#sec-robust}

## Starting in 1980 instead of 1959 {#sec-robust-sample}

The 146 targets are identical in the two runs. What differs is the training data: 40 against 121 quarters before the first target, and no 1960s or 1970s. Each change therefore mixes two effects: dropping data whose errors may be unrepresentative, and estimating parameters from less history.

**What survives.** m13 is first on every target on both samples. Serially correlated errors help on both samples, with and without SV; in the constant-variance comparison they help in every sub-period (@tbl-sub). m13's AR(1) coefficients barely move (@tbl-post). The structural restriction is still unsupported. Production remains the cleanest measure in every specification. m10's lead over m8 is essentially unchanged (`r sg(pw(PW8, "m10", "m8", comp = G2))`, z `r fmt(pw(PW8, "m10", "m8", "z_nw", G2), 2)`). m13's latent path is almost the same: on the common quarters the posterior mean paths have correlation `r fmt(rob("m13_full", "m13_prod", "mu_mean_cor"), 4)` and differ by `r fmt(rob("m13_full", "m13_prod", "mu_mean_mad"), 2)` points on average (at most `r fmt(rob("m13_full", "m13_prod", "mu_mean_max"), 2)`).

**What weakens.** The latent-SV evidence: m13 − m12 is `r sg(pw(PW8, "m13", "m12"))` with z `r fmt(z138, 2)`. Newey-West z-statistics at lags 4, 8, 12 and 16 are `r paste(fmt(lagz(d13128), 2), collapse = ", ")` (full sample `r paste(fmt(lagz(d1312f), 2), collapse = ", ")`). The z ≥ 2 condition that was used to switch production to m13 (@sec-app-history) would not be met on this sample. Part of the 1980 margin is in 2021–22 (`r sg(fv("m13", "m12", "2021-22", "diff_sample"))`, against `r sg(fv("m13", "m12", "2021-22"))` on the full sample). In that period m12's 1980 fit mishandles the aftermath of COVID (below), so part of the margin scores that failure rather than a general gain. Measurement SV also weakens: the nested gains roughly halve (@tbl-pairs).

**Why the measurement-SV gain halves.** Before 2020 every model scores better when trained from 1980, but the constant-variance models gain about twice as much. Their error variances, GDP(E)'s above all, are no longer inflated by the noisy early decades. The pre-2020 change from the later start is `r sg(fvsm_pre <- (sum(LP8$elpd[LP8$model == "m2" & as.Date(LP8$date) < as.Date("2020-01-01")]) - sum(LPf$elpd[LPf$model == "m2" & as.Date(LPf$date) < as.Date("2020-01-01")])))` for m2 against `r sg(sum(LP8$elpd[LP8$model == "m4" & as.Date(LP8$date) < as.Date("2020-01-01")]) - sum(LPf$elpd[LPf$model == "m4" & as.Date(LPf$date) < as.Date("2020-01-01")]))` for m4. In the constant-variance models the expenditure error standard deviation falls from `r fmt(pv("m2_full", "sigma[1]"), 2)` to `r fmt(pv("m2_1980", "sigma[1]"), 2)` (m2). That is the pattern RDP 2014-12's argument for a 1980 start predicts. About half of the full-sample measurement-SV gain came from pre-1980 training data. The rest survives the later start, but less cleanly: before 2020 the nested gains are `r sg(fv("m4", "m2", "pre-2020", "diff_sample"))` and `r sg(fv("m9", "m6", "pre-2020", "diff_sample"))` on the 1980 sample against `r sg(fv("m4", "m2", "pre-2020"))` and `r sg(fv("m9", "m6", "pre-2020"))` on the full sample, and the 1980 fits of m4 and m9 lose to the constant-variance models in 2021–22 (`r fmt(fv("m4", "m2", "2021-22", "diff_sample"), 1)` and `r fmt(fv("m9", "m6", "2021-22", "diff_sample"), 1)`).

**What fails: m4, m9 and m12 on COVID.** On the 1980 sample these three models, which have measurement SV but a constant latent variance, treat the 2020 Q2 collapse as a common measurement error (@fig-covid). Their latent growth in 2020 Q2 is `r fmt(cov("m4_1980"), 1)` (m4), `r fmt(cov("m9_1980"), 1)` (m9) and `r fmt(cov("m12_1980"), 1)` (m12), against `r fmt(cov("m4_full"), 1)`, `r fmt(cov("m9_full"), 1)` and `r fmt(cov("m12_full"), 1)` on the full sample and a headline of `r fmt(hl_2020q2, 1)`. Their variance ratios fall to `r fmt(min(sapply(paste0(c("m4","m9","m12"), "_1980"), vr, w = "1980Q1-2026Q2")), 2)`–`r fmt(max(sapply(paste0(c("m4","m9","m12"), "_1980"), vr, w = "1980Q1-2026Q2")), 2)`. This is the same failure as the old m10's mode A. In m12 the expenditure-volatility persistence collapses to `r pci("m12_1980", "phi[1]")`, against `r pci("m12_full", "phi[1]")` on the full sample, while its volatility of volatility rises to `r fmt(pv("m12_1980", "omega[1]"), 2)`. Expenditure-side SV then behaves as i.i.d. heavy-tailed noise that can absorb one huge quarter. The prior on that persistence is Uniform(−1, 1), so a posterior centred near zero with a wide interval is close to the prior. We checked that this is not a stranded mode. For each of m4, m9 and m12, four extra chains were started from full-sample draws, where COVID is in latent growth. All twelve chains moved to the measurement-error solution and matched the reference fit. Warmup draws were saved for m4 and m12, and there every chain left the starting region within `r fact("mode_check_1980_first_iter_min")` to `r fact("mode_check_1980_first_iter_max")` warmup iterations. That is evidence about one alternative region, not proof that no other mode exists. m13 and m10, which have latent SV, keep COVID in latent growth on both samples. So, mostly, do the constant-variance models: their latent 2020 Q2 is `r fmt(min(sapply(paste0(c("m1","m2","m3","m5","m6"), "_1980"), cov)), 1)` to `r fmt(max(sapply(paste0(c("m1","m2","m3","m5","m6"), "_1980"), cov)), 1)` on the 1980 sample.

```{r}
#| label: fig-covid
#| fig-cap: "Latent growth in 2020 Q2 by model and sample: posterior mean and 90% interval, annualised per cent. Dashed line: headline growth in 2020 Q2. m11's value is the quarterly aggregate of its monthly state."
cv <- COV[COV$key %in% c(paste0("m", 1:13, "_full"), paste0("m", 1:13, "_1980")), ]
cv$model <- factor(cv$model, levels = rev(paste0("m", 1:13)))
cv$Sample <- ifelse(cv$sample == "full", "Full sample", "1980 sample")
p6 <- ggplot(cv, aes(y = model, x = mu_mean, colour = Sample)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = hl_2020q2, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = mu_q05, xmax = mu_q95), position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), size = 0.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(NULL, values = c("Full sample" = "grey30", "1980 sample" = "#d7301f")) +
  labs(x = "latent growth in 2020 Q2, % (annualised)", y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 9) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
f6 <- "figures/fig6_covid_by_model.png"
ggsave(f6, p6, width = 6.5, height = 3.8, dpi = 200)
knitr::include_graphics(f6)
```

**What changes.** m7 rises from sixth to fourth on the 1980 sample, level with m9 and m4. m13's variance ratio is higher on the 1980 sample, but only because the window excludes the 1960s and 1970s (@sec-vardecomp).

**Does the later start improve prediction?** m13 trained from 1980 scores `r sg(FVSM$change[FVSM$model == "m13"])` nats better on the same 146 targets than m13 trained from 1959 (NW SE `r fmt(FVSM$se_nw_change[FVSM$model == "m13"], 2)`, z `r fmt(FVSM$change[FVSM$model == "m13"] / FVSM$se_nw_change[FVSM$model == "m13"], 2)`). Most of the gain is in 1990–99 (`r sg(sum(ds_9099))`). These are the targets nearest the dropped data, and they have the shortest 1980 training sets. From 2000 on the gain is `r sg(sum(ds_2000))` (z `r fmt(sum(ds_2000) / nw(ds_2000), 2)`). For current estimates the start date hardly matters for prediction. The published estimate moved to the 1980 sample on 19 October 2026. That was a decision based on RDP 2014-12's argument about early measurement errors, not the outcome of a pre-set rule (@sec-app-history).

## Prior sensitivity

The posterior median of $\omega_g$ on the full sample (`r fmt(pv("m13_full", "omega_g"), 2)`) sits at percentile `r fmt(100 * (2 * pnorm(pv("m13_full", "omega_g") / 0.5) - 1), 0)` of its half-N(0, 0.5) prior. On the 1980 sample (`r fmt(pv("m13_prod", "omega_g"), 2)`) it sits at percentile `r fmt(100 * (2 * pnorm(pv("m13_prod", "omega_g") / 0.5) - 1), 0)`. The prior may therefore restrain it. We refitted the full-sample m13 with a half-N(0, 1) prior; the refit also passed the gate. $\omega_g$ moved from `r pci("m13_full", "omega_g")` to `r pci("m13_full_omegag1", "omega_g")`, and $\tau$ from `r fmt(pv("m13_full", "tau"), 2)` to `r fmt(pv("m13_full_omegag1", "tau"), 2)`. The median $\tau_t$ path changed by `r pc(rob("m13_full", "m13_full_omegag1", "tau_median_rel_mean"), 1)` on average (at most `r pc(rob("m13_full", "m13_full_omegag1", "tau_median_rel_max"), 1)`). The median latent path moved by `r fmt(rob("m13_full", "m13_full_omegag1", "mu_median_mad"), 3)` points on average (at most `r fmt(rob("m13_full", "m13_full_omegag1", "mu_median_max"), 2)`). The variance ratio went from `r fmt(vr("m13_full", "1959Q4-2026Q2"), 3)` to `r fmt(vr("m13_full_omegag1", "1959Q4-2026Q2"), 3)`. The results are insensitive to this widening.

For this paper the same refit was run on the production sample, 1980 Q1 to 2026 Q2 (`R/fit_m13.R --omega_g_sd=1`). There the prior matters more, because the 1980 posterior of $\omega_g$ sits further into the prior's tail. The refit `r ifelse(all(G1O$pass), "passed", "did not pass")` the production gate (`r nd1 <- round(G1O$value[grepl("divergences", G1O$metric)] * 8000); nd1` divergence`r ifelse(nd1 == 1, "", "s")`, minimum E-BFMI `r fmt(G1O$value[grepl("E-BFMI", G1O$metric)], 3)`, maximum hyperparameter R-hat `r fmt(G1O$value[grepl("max R-hat, hyperparameters", G1O$metric)], 4)`, minimum hyperparameter bulk ESS `r fmt(G1O$value[grepl("min bulk ESS, hyperparameters", G1O$metric)], 0)`). $\omega_g$ moved from `r pci("m13_prod", "omega_g")` to `r pci("m13_1980_omegag1", "omega_g")`, $\phi_g$ from `r fmt(pv("m13_prod", "phi_g"), 2)` to `r fmt(pv("m13_1980_omegag1", "phi_g"), 2)` and $\tau$ from `r fmt(pv("m13_prod", "tau"), 2)` to `r fmt(pv("m13_1980_omegag1", "tau"), 2)`. The median $\tau_t$ path changed by `r pc(rob("m13_prod", "m13_1980_omegag1", "tau_median_rel_mean"), 1)` on average (at most `r pc(rob("m13_prod", "m13_1980_omegag1", "tau_median_rel_max"), 1)`, in `r qlab(rob("m13_prod", "m13_1980_omegag1", "tau_median_rel_max_date"))`); 2020 Q2's $\tau_t$ went from `r fmt(mp("m13_prod", q2, "tau_q50"), 1)` to `r fmt(mp("m13_1980_omegag1", q2, "tau_q50"), 1)`. The median latent path moved by `r fmt(rob("m13_prod", "m13_1980_omegag1", "mu_median_mad"), 3)` points on average (at most `r fmt(rob("m13_prod", "m13_1980_omegag1", "mu_median_max"), 2)`), and the variance ratio went from `r fmt(vr("m13_prod", "1980Q1-2026Q2"), 3)` to `r fmt(vr("m13_1980_omegag1", "1980Q1-2026Q2"), 3)` (`r fmt(vr("m13_prod", "1980Q1-2026Q2 excl. 2020Q1-2021Q1"), 3)` to `r fmt(vr("m13_1980_omegag1", "1980Q1-2026Q2 excl. 2020Q1-2021Q1"), 3)` excluding 2020 Q1–2021 Q1). The latent path and the variance ratio are again insensitive. The latent-volatility path is less so: it moves by up to a sixth in some quarters, so statements about $\tau_t$ in individual quarters carry prior uncertainty beyond their posterior intervals. The wider prior was not scored by LFO.

### Tighter priors {#sec-robust-priors}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-tight
#| tbl-cap: "m13 with its own priors (the production fit) and with the tighter priors chosen in @sec-ppc, both on 1980 Q1–2026 Q2, seed 1 (seed 2 of the variant in the last column). Posterior medians and 90% intervals, annualised units. Variance ratio: per-draw var(μ)/var(headline). $\\tau_t$ by decade: posterior median of the decade average. Diagnostics: the production gate (all checks passed for all three fits); time is the wall time of the sampler with four parallel chains on a six-core machine, which also ran other work."
k0 <- "m13_prod"; k1 <- "m13t_1980"; k2 <- "m13t_1980_seed2"
pcell <- function(k, v, d = 2) paste(fmt(pv(k, v), d), ci(pv(k, v, "q05"), pv(k, v, "q95"), d))
mcell <- function(k, dt, a = "mu") paste(fmt(mp(k, dt, paste0(a, "_q50")), 2), ci(mp(k, dt, paste0(a, "_q05")), mp(k, dt, paste0(a, "_q95")), 2))
vcell <- function(k, w) paste(fmt(vr(k, w), 3), ci(vr(k, w, "ratio_q05"), vr(k, w, "ratio_q95"), 3))
gcell <- function(k) paste0(round(gtt(k, "divergences") * 8000), " div; E-BFMI ", fmt(gtt(k, "min E-BFMI"), 3), "; R-hat ", fmt(gtt(k, "max R-hat, hyperparameters"), 4),
                            "; ESS ", fmt(gtt(k, "min bulk ESS, hyperparameters"), 0), "/", fmt(gtt(k, "min tail ESS, hyperparameters"), 0), " (", gtt(k, "min bulk ESS, hyperparameters", "worst"), ")")
tcell <- function(k) paste(fmt(GTT$wall_secs[GTT$key == k][1] / 60, 1), "min")
rows <- list(
  c("$\\rho$", "rho"), c("$\\bar\\mu$", "mu_bar"), c("$\\tau = e^{\\mu_g/2}$", "tau"), c("$\\phi_g$", "phi_g"), c("$\\omega_g$", "omega_g"),
  c("$\\phi_E$", "phi[1]"), c("$\\phi_I$", "phi[2]"), c("$\\phi_P$", "phi[3]"), c("$\\omega_E$", "omega[1]"), c("$\\omega_I$", "omega[2]"), c("$\\omega_P$", "omega[3]"),
  c("$\\psi_E$", "psi[1]"), c("$\\psi_I$", "psi[2]"), c("$\\psi_P$", "psi[3]"), c("$\\rho_{EI}$", "rho_EI"))
tt <- rbind(
  do.call(rbind, lapply(rows, function(r) data.frame(Quantity = r[1], m13 = pcell(k0, r[2]), Tight = pcell(k1, r[2]), `Tight, seed 2` = pcell(k2, r[2]), check.names = FALSE))),
  data.frame(Quantity = c(paste("latent growth,", qlab(last)), "latent growth, 2020 Q2", "$\\tau_t$, 2020 Q2",
                          "variance ratio, 1980 Q1–2026 Q2", "variance ratio, excl. 2020 Q1–2021 Q1"),
             m13 = c(mcell(k0, last), mcell(k0, q2), mcell(k0, q2, "tau"), vcell(k0, "1980Q1-2026Q2"), vcell(k0, "1980Q1-2026Q2 excl. 2020Q1-2021Q1")),
             Tight = c(mcell(k1, last), mcell(k1, q2), mcell(k1, q2, "tau"), vcell(k1, "1980Q1-2026Q2"), vcell(k1, "1980Q1-2026Q2 excl. 2020Q1-2021Q1")),
             `Tight, seed 2` = c(mcell(k2, last), mcell(k2, q2), mcell(k2, q2, "tau"), vcell(k2, "1980Q1-2026Q2"), vcell(k2, "1980Q1-2026Q2 excl. 2020Q1-2021Q1")), check.names = FALSE),
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c("1980s", "1990s", "2000s", "2010s", "2020s"), function(dd) data.frame(Quantity = paste("$\\tau_t$,", dd),
             m13 = paste(fmt(dec(k0, dd), 2), ci(dec(k0, dd, "q05"), dec(k0, dd, "q95"), 2)), Tight = paste(fmt(dec(k1, dd), 2), ci(dec(k1, dd, "q05"), dec(k1, dd, "q95"), 2)),
             `Tight, seed 2` = paste(fmt(dec(k2, dd), 2), ci(dec(k2, dd, "q05"), dec(k2, dd, "q95"), 2)), check.names = FALSE))),
  data.frame(Quantity = c("diagnostics", "time"), m13 = c(gcell(k0), tcell(k0)), Tight = c(gcell(k1), tcell(k1)), `Tight, seed 2` = c(gcell(k2), tcell(k2)), check.names = FALSE))
tab(tt, align = "lrrr")
```

The prior predictive check of @sec-ppc chose a set of tighter priors (C3: a Beta(2.625, 2.625) prior on $\rho$, N(3, 2) on $\bar\mu$, and half-N(0, 1) on the stationary standard deviation of each log-variance). We fitted this variant to the production sample with the production settings and evaluated it with the production gate. It passed on both seeds (@tbl-tight); the two seeds agree as closely as m13's seeds do (median latent paths `r fmt(rob(k1, k2, "mu_median_mad"), 3)` points apart on average, `r fmt(rob(k1, k2, "mu_median_max"), 2)` at most). Its sampler took `r fmt(GTT$wall_secs[GTT$key == k1][1] / 60, 0)` and `r fmt(GTT$wall_secs[GTT$key == k2][1] / 60, 0)` minutes against `r fmt(GTT$wall_secs[GTT$key == k0][1] / 60, 0)` and `r fmt(GTT$wall_secs[GTT$key == "m13_1980_seed2"][1] / 60, 0)` for m13's two seeds; the machine was shared with other work, so we read this only as "no slower".

**What does not move.** The latent path, the measurement-error parameters and the variance split are essentially unchanged. The median latent path moves by `r fmt(rob(k0, k1, "mu_median_mad"), 3)` annualised points on average and by at most `r fmt(rob(k0, k1, "mu_median_max"), 2)` (in `r qlab(rob(k0, k1, "mu_median_max_date"))`), against a seed-to-seed difference for m13 of `r fmt(rob("m13_prod", "m13_1980_seed2", "mu_median_mad"), 3)` on average and `r fmt(rob("m13_prod", "m13_1980_seed2", "mu_median_max"), 2)` at most. Latent growth in `r qlab(last)` is `r fmt(mp(k1, last, "mu_q50") / 4, 2)` per cent quarter-on-quarter (90% interval `r fmt(mp(k1, last, "mu_q05") / 4, 2)` to `r fmt(mp(k1, last, "mu_q95") / 4, 2)`), against `r fmt(mp(k0, last, "mu_q50") / 4, 2)` (`r fmt(mp(k0, last, "mu_q05") / 4, 2)` to `r fmt(mp(k0, last, "mu_q95") / 4, 2)`). The per-draw variance ratio is `r fmt(vr(k1, "1980Q1-2026Q2"), 3)` against `r fmt(vr(k0, "1980Q1-2026Q2"), 3)`, and `r fmt(vr(k1, "1980Q1-2026Q2 excl. 2020Q1-2021Q1"), 3)` against `r fmt(vr(k0, "1980Q1-2026Q2 excl. 2020Q1-2021Q1"), 3)` excluding 2020 Q1–2021 Q1. $\rho$, $\bar\mu$, $\psi$ and $\rho_{EI}$ move by a few hundredths at most. In the error block the only visible change is that the long left tail of the expenditure-volatility persistence $\phi_E$ (@sec-results) shortens: its 5% point rises from `r fmt(pv(k0, "phi[1]", "q05"), 2)` to `r fmt(pv(k1, "phi[1]", "q05"), 2)`. The Beta prior's exclusion of negative $\rho$ does not bind: m13's 90% interval for $\rho$ is already well inside (0, 1). The posterior predictive checks give the same picture as m13's (@tbl-ppc): in the full replication the p-values lie between `r fmt(min(PPCT$p_rep_ge_obs[PPCT$kind == "full"]), 2)` and `r fmt(max(PPCT$p_rep_ge_obs[PPCT$kind == "full"]), 2)`, the observed pre-2020 headline standard deviation is below `r pc(ppct("full", "sd_head_pre2020"))` of replications, and the conditional 90% intervals cover `r pc(PPVT$cover90[PPVT$measure == "E"])`, `r pc(PPVT$cover90[PPVT$measure == "I"])` and `r pc(PPVT$cover90[PPVT$measure == "P"])` of the observations. The replications' upper tails are thinner: the 95th percentile of the replicated headline standard deviation is `r fmt(ppct("full", "sd_head", "q95"), 1)` against `r fmt(ppc("full", "sd_head", "q95"), 1)` under m13's priors.

**What moves.** The latent-volatility block. Latent log-volatility is less persistent and more variable ($\phi_g$ `r pci(k1, "phi_g")` against `r pci(k0, "phi_g")`; $\omega_g$ `r pci(k1, "omega_g")` against `r pci(k0, "omega_g")`), and $\tau$ is a little lower (`r fmt(pv(k1, "tau"), 2)` against `r fmt(pv(k0, "tau"), 2)`). The median $\tau_t$ path changes by `r pc(rob(k0, k1, "tau_median_rel_mean"), 1)` on average and by up to `r pc(rob(k0, k1, "tau_median_rel_max"), 0)` (in `r qlab(rob(k0, k1, "tau_median_rel_max_date"))`); 2020 Q2's $\tau_t$ goes from `r fmt(mp(k0, q2, "tau_q50"), 1)` to `r fmt(mp(k1, q2, "tau_q50"), 1)`. The decade averages move by at most `r fmt(max(abs(sapply(c("1980s", "1990s", "2000s", "2010s", "2020s"), function(dd) dec(k1, dd) - dec(k0, dd)))), 2)` (@tbl-tight). This is the same direction and size as the half-N(0, 1) prior on $\omega_g$ above, and for the same reason: the prior on the scale of the latent log-variance restrains it. The posterior median of $s_g$, `r fmt(pv(k1, "s_g"), 2)`, is at the `r fmt(100 * (2 * pnorm(pv(k1, "s_g")) - 1), 0)`th percentile of its half-N(0, 1) prior. Statements about $\tau_t$ in single quarters are therefore prior-sensitive at the level of a fifth; the latent path and the variance split are not.

**On RDP 2014-12's sample.** On 1980 Q1–2013 Q2 (`paper/fit_rdp_sample.R m13_tight`) the variant does not identify latent-volatility persistence any better: $\phi_g$ is `r pci("m13t_rdp", "phi_g")` against `r pci("m13_rdp", "phi_g")` under m13's priors, and $s_g$ is `r pci("m13t_rdp", "s_g")`. Without COVID the latent log-variance varies too little for its persistence to be learnt from 134 quarters, and the Uniform(−1, 1) prior on $\phi_g$ was kept. The median latent path moves by `r fmt(rob("m13_rdp", "m13t_rdp", "mu_median_mad"), 3)` points on average (at most `r fmt(rob("m13_rdp", "m13t_rdp", "mu_median_max"), 2)`) and the variance ratio over 1980–2013 is `r fmt(vr("m13t_rdp", wR8 <- "1980Q1-2013Q2"), 3)` against `r fmt(vr("m13_rdp", wR8), 3)`. That fit had `r RDPD$divergences[RDPD$model == "m13_tight"]` divergences, minimum E-BFMI `r fmt(RDPD$min_ebfmi[RDPD$model == "m13_tight"], 2)`, maximum hyperparameter R-hat `r fmt(RDPD$max_rhat_hyper[RDPD$model == "m13_tight"], 4)` (on `r RDPD$worst_rhat_var[RDPD$model == "m13_tight"]`) and minimum hyperparameter bulk ESS `r fmt(RDPD$min_ess_bulk_hyper[RDPD$model == "m13_tight"], 0)`.

The variant was not scored by LFO. Since the latent path and the variance split do not move, and the production model was chosen by LFO under m13's priors, we see no result here that would change a published number beyond the latent-volatility path. Production keeps m13's priors.

## Seeds

```{r}
#| label: tbl-seeds
#| tbl-cap: "Seed robustness of m13: second-seed fits against seed 1. Path differences are in annualised percentage points; $\\tau_t$ differences are relative changes of the posterior median."
sd <- data.frame(
  Sample = c("Full", "1980"),
  `Gate passed (seed 2)` = c(ifelse(all(G13f$pass[G13f$seed == 2]), "yes", "no"), ifelse(all(G138$pass[G138$seed == 2]), "yes", "no")),
  `Median $\\mu$ path: mean / max abs. Δ` = c(paste(fmt(rob("m13_full", "m13_full_seed2", "mu_median_mad"), 3), "/", fmt(rob("m13_full", "m13_full_seed2", "mu_median_max"), 3)),
                                       paste(fmt(rob("m13_prod", "m13_1980_seed2", "mu_median_mad"), 3), "/", fmt(rob("m13_prod", "m13_1980_seed2", "mu_median_max"), 3))),
  `Median $\\tau_t$: mean / max rel. Δ` = c(paste(pc(rob("m13_full", "m13_full_seed2", "tau_median_rel_mean"), 1), "/", pc(rob("m13_full", "m13_full_seed2", "tau_median_rel_max"), 1)),
                                      paste(pc(rob("m13_prod", "m13_1980_seed2", "tau_median_rel_mean"), 1), "/", pc(rob("m13_prod", "m13_1980_seed2", "tau_median_rel_max"), 1))),
  `Variance ratio, seed 1 / seed 2` = c(paste(fmt(vr("m13_full", "1959Q4-2026Q2"), 3), "/", fmt(vr("m13_full_seed2", "1959Q4-2026Q2"), 3)),
                                        paste(fmt(vr("m13_prod", "1980Q1-2026Q2"), 3), "/", fmt(vr("m13_1980_seed2", "1980Q1-2026Q2"), 3))),
  `$\\psi_E$, seed 1 / seed 2` = c(paste(fmt(pv("m13_full", "psi[1]"), 3), "/", fmt(pv("m13_full_seed2", "psi[1]"), 3)),
                            paste(fmt(pv("m13_prod", "psi[1]"), 3), "/", fmt(pv("m13_1980_seed2", "psi[1]"), 3))),
  check.names = FALSE)
tab(sd, align = "llrrrr")
```

@tbl-seeds compares second-seed fits with seed 1. Both pass the gate, and the latent path, the volatility path and the variance ratio agree to within Monte Carlo noise.

## Refit retries and seed selection

```{r retry}
nfit_f <- sum(MCf$n_fits); nfit_8 <- sum(MC8$n_fits); nref_f <- sum(MCf$n_refits); nref_8 <- sum(MC8$n_refits)
fail_f <- sum(MCf$n_attempts_failed); fail_8 <- sum(MC8$n_attempts_failed)
wk_f <- sum(MCf$n_fits_weak_mixing); wk_8 <- sum(MC8$n_fits_weak_mixing)
```

On the full sample all `r nfit_f` stored LFO fits (`r nrow(MCf)` initial fits and `r nref_f` refits) meet the refit rule. `r sum(MCf$n_fits_retried)` of them met it only after `r fail_f` failed attempts. The retried fits are m9 on data to 2006 Q3 and to 2020 Q4, and m12 on data to 2020 Q4. Just after COVID, four chains of 1,000 draws do not sample the latent variance reliably in the constant-latent-variance models. On the 1980 sample all `r nfit_8` fits meet the rule and one (m4, on data to 2016 Q2) needed a second attempt. `r wk_f` full-sample and `r wk_8` 1980-sample fits meet the rule but have bulk ESS below 400. Rescoring without seed selection changes the key comparisons little. m13 − m12 on the full sample is `r sg(rs(RSf, "m13", "m12", "main"), 2)` as reported, `r sg(rs(RSf, "m13", "m12", "first"), 2)` with first attempts only (z `r fmt(rs(RSf, "m13", "m12", "first", "z_nw"), 2)`), and `r sg(rs(RSf, "m13", "m12", "pooled"), 2)` with all attempts pooled. m12 − m9 is `r sg(rs(RSf, "m12", "m9", "main"), 2)`, `r sg(rs(RSf, "m12", "m9", "first"), 2)` (z `r fmt(rs(RSf, "m12", "m9", "first", "z_nw"), 2)`) and `r sg(rs(RSf, "m12", "m9", "pooled"), 2)`. On the 1980 sample m4 − m2 is `r sg(rs(RS8, "m4", "m2", "main"), 1)` as reported and `r sg(rs(RS8, "m4", "m2", "first"), 1)` with first attempts only. m13 needed no retry on either sample. The largest Pareto $\hat k$ used without a refit was `r fmt(max(MCf$max_k_used, MC8$max_k_used), 4)`, below the 0.7 threshold.

## Particle-filter accuracy {#sec-robust-pf}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pf
#| tbl-cap: "Particle-filter bias against high-particle references (nats), summed over 2020 Q1–2021 Q1 (COVID) and over 2015 Q1–2019 Q4. 'Schedule' is the adaptive particle count used for scoring; 'N = 2000' a fixed count. COVID biases use the mean of three reference passes at 2020 Q2. MCSE: Monte Carlo SE of the model's total score."
pfr <- function(PFC, PFP, MC, m, s) {
  a <- PFC[PFC$model == m, ]; b <- PFP[PFP$model == m, ]
  data.frame(Sample = s, Model = m, `COVID, schedule` = fmt(sum(a$bias_sched_vs_refmean), 2), `COVID, N = 2000` = fmt(sum(a$bias_N2000_vs_refmean), 2),
             `2015–19, schedule` = if (nrow(b)) fmt(sum(b$bias_sched), 3) else "not run",
             `2020 Q2 reference SE` = fmt(a$elpd_ref_se[a$date == "2020-06-01"], 3),
             MCSE = fmt(mc(MC, m, "mcse_elpd"), 2), check.names = FALSE)
}
tpf <- rbind(do.call(rbind, lapply(c("m13", "m12", "m9", "m4", "m10"), pfr, PFC = PFCf, PFP = PFPf, MC = MCf, s = "Full")),
             do.call(rbind, lapply(c("m13", "m12", "m9", "m4"), pfr, PFC = PFC8, PFP = PFP8, MC = MC8, s = "1980")))
tab(tpf, align = "llrrrrr")
```

@tbl-pf reports the particle-filter checks. Under the adaptive schedule the bias summed over the COVID quarters is small for every model on the full sample. A fixed 2,000-particle filter would have been biased by a few tenths of a nat, downwards for every model except m10 (`r sg(sum(PFCf$bias_N2000_vs_refmean[PFCf$model == "m10"]), 2)`). The 1980 sample is harder. For the three models that treat COVID as measurement error, the 2020 Q2 predictive density needs all three measurement volatilities to jump at once. Its estimate varies by more than a nat between passes even at 100,000 particles, and a fixed 2,000-particle filter would be biased by about −3 nats. Comparisons involving m4, m9 or m12 on the 1980 sample therefore carry one to two nats of particle uncertainty from that quarter. That is small against m13 − m12 but not against m9 − m4. For m13 the 2020 Q2 reference has a standard error of `r fmt(PFC8$elpd_ref_se[PFC8$model == "m13" & PFC8$date == "2020-06-01"], 3)` nats on the 1980 sample, and its total MCSE is `r fmt(mc(MC8, "m13", "mcse_elpd"), 2)`. With four passes each MCSE has only three degrees of freedom. The checks for 2015–19 were not run for m9 (1980 sample), m4 or m10, and the COVID check was not run for m10 on the 1980 sample.

## Mode checks

Besides the m10 diagnosis (@sec-failed) and the 1980-sample restarts of m4, m9 and m12 (@sec-robust-sample), the m13 fits show no sign of multiple modes. All four chains of each fit agree (maximum hyperparameter R-hat `r fmt(max(G13f$value[grepl("max R-hat, hyperparameters", G13f$metric)], G138$value[grepl("max R-hat, hyperparameters", G138$metric)]), 4)` across both samples and seeds), and the two seeds agree (@tbl-seeds). Tempered or optimisation-based searches for other modes were not run.

# Relation to RDP 2014-12 {#sec-rdp}

RDP 2014-12 is the starting point of this project. This section sets out what differs between the two studies. It then reports a re-estimation of six of our models on RDP 2014-12's sample period, which makes part of the comparison like-for-like.

**What differs.**

* **Sample end and vintage.** RDP 2014-12 use data from 1980 Q1 to 2013 Q2, on the vintage available in 2014. Our 1980 sample has the same start but ends in 2026 Q2, on the 2026 vintage. It therefore includes the COVID quarters and thirteen years of revisions to the earlier data. The re-estimation below uses their sample period on our vintage.
* **Fourth signal.** Their Model 3 adds the change in the unemployment rate. Our m8 and m10 are in the spirit of that model but add hours worked; we have not used unemployment.
* **Error correlations.** Their Model 2 lets the latent innovation correlate with each measurement error and identifies the model by fixing the ratio of latent to GDP(E) variance at 0.5. None of our models has latent–error correlation, and our m3 (errors only, LKJ prior) does not impose that restriction.
* **Variances.** Their models have constant variances. Our preferred models have stochastic volatility in latent growth and in the errors, and AR(1) errors.
* **Units and priors.** They work in quarterly percentages with inverse-gamma priors on variances and a beta prior on persistence. We work in annualised percentages with half-normal priors on standard deviations and a truncated normal on persistence.
* **Estimation and evaluation.** They use random-walk Metropolis-Hastings; they report marginal data densities but do not use them to choose between models. We use HMC and compare models by leave-future-out predictive density.
* **Real-time analysis.** They evaluate revisions to real-time model estimates from 2001 to 2009. We use the current vintage only.

## Re-estimation on the RDP sample {#sec-rdp-refit}

```{r rdp-setup}
RDPD <- rd("../output/sample_rdp/tables/fit_diagnostics.csv")
E19D <- if (file.exists("../output/sample_rdp/end2019/tables/fit_diagnostics.csv")) rd("../output/sample_rdp/end2019/tables/fit_diagnostics.csv") else RDPD[0, ]
DALL <- rbind(RDPD[RDPD$model != "m13_tight", ], E19D)   # the tighter-prior variant is reported in @sec-robust-priors
q <- function(x) x / 4
wR <- "1980Q1-2013Q2"
taubar <- function(key) mean(M13$tau_q50[M13$key == key & M13$date <= as.Date("2013-06-01")]) / 4
r5 <- function(s, c) R5[R5$series == s, c]
r4 <- function(s, c) R4[R4$series == s, c]
sdr <- function(key) r5(key, "sd") / r5("headline", "sd")
m6 <- c("m2", "m4", "m5", "m9", "m12", "m13")
key80 <- function(m) if (m == "m13") "m13_prod" else paste0(m, "_1980")
vr_rdp <- sapply(paste0(m6, "_rdp"), vr, w = wR)
sdr_rdp <- sapply(paste0(m6, "_rdp"), sdr)
```

We refitted m2, m4, m5, m9, m12 and m13 on 1980 Q1 to 2013 Q2 (T = 134), on the 2026 vintage, with the production sampler settings (`paper/fit_rdp_sample.R`). To separate the effect of the COVID quarters from that of the 2013–19 data, m2 and m13 were also fitted on 1980 Q1 to 2019 Q4. Across the `r nrow(DALL)` fits there was at most `r max(DALL$divergences)` divergence in 8,000 draws, a minimum E-BFMI of `r fmt(min(DALL$min_ebfmi), 2)` and a minimum hyperparameter bulk ESS of `r fmt(min(DALL$min_ess_bulk_hyper), 0)`. The largest hyperparameter R-hat is `r fmt(max(DALL$max_rhat_hyper), 4)` (m13 to 2019 Q4, on the persistence of the production-error volatility), just above the production gate's 1.01; the m13 fit to 2013 Q2 has `r fmt(RDPD$max_rhat_hyper[RDPD$model == "m13"], 4)`. On these shorter samples m13's latent-volatility parameters are weakly identified: on 1980 Q1–2013 Q2, $\phi_g$ is `r pci("m13_rdp", "phi_g")` and $\omega_g$ `r pci("m13_rdp", "omega_g")`, against `r pci("m13_prod", "omega_g")` when 2020–26 is included. Each fit took at most `r fmt(max(DALL$wall_secs) / 60, 0)` minutes. No LFO comparison was run on these samples.

Their Model 1, an AR(1) latent state with independent constant-variance errors, has the same structure as our m2 except for priors. @tbl-rdp sets the two side by side. All numbers are in quarterly units: our annualised estimates divided by four. Panel B describes the posterior-median latent path over RDP 2014-12's window, 1980 Q1 to 2013 Q2, whatever the end of the estimation sample.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-rdp
#| tbl-cap: "RDP 2014-12's Model 1 against our m2 and m13 fitted on three sample ends, quarterly units (per cent per quarter). RDP: values as published (Tables 1, 4 and 5; sample 1980 Q1–2013 Q2; sds are square roots of median variances). Ours: posterior medians, all samples starting in 1980 Q1, 2026 vintage. Panels B and C are computed over 1980 Q1–2013 Q2 for every column. For m13 the latent sd is the average median $\\tau_t$ over 1980 Q1–2013 Q2 and the error sds are $\\bar\\sigma^\\varepsilon_k$ (at the long-run log-variance), so they are not like-for-like with constant-variance sds. In Panel B the sd of GDP(A) is RDP 2014-12's value (2014 vintage) and ours (2026 vintage)."
cols <- list(c("m2_rdp", "m2, to 2013 Q2"), c("m2_e2019", "m2, to 2019 Q4"), c("m2_1980", "m2, to 2026 Q2"),
             c("m13_rdp", "m13, to 2013 Q2"), c("m13_e2019", "m13, to 2019 Q4"), c("m13_prod", "m13, to 2026 Q2"))
cols <- Filter(function(cc) any(P$key == cc[1]), cols)
colA <- function(key) {
  if (grepl("^m2", key)) c(pv(key, "rho"), q(pv(key, "tau")), q(pv(key, "sigma[1]")), q(pv(key, "sigma[2]")), q(pv(key, "sigma[3]")), q(pv(key, "mu_bar")))
  else c(pv(key, "rho"), taubar(key), q(pv(key, "eps_sd_bar[1]")), q(pv(key, "eps_sd_bar[2]")), q(pv(key, "eps_sd_bar[3]")), q(pv(key, "mu_bar")))
}
colB <- function(key) c(r5("headline", "sd"), r5(key, "sd"), sdr(key), r5(key, "rho1"), vr(key, wR), vr(key, wR, "ratio_medianpath"))
colC <- function(key) c(r4(key, "w_E"), r4(key, "w_I"), r4(key, "w_P"))
rdpA <- c(rdpv(1, "Model 1", "rho"), sqrt(rdpv(1, "Model 1", "sigma2_G")), sqrt(rdpv(1, "Model 1", "sigma2_E")),
          sqrt(rdpv(1, "Model 1", "sigma2_I")), sqrt(rdpv(1, "Model 1", "sigma2_P")), rdpv(1, "Model 1", "mu"))
rdpB <- c(rdpv(5, "GDP(A)", "sd", "value"), rdpv(5, "Model 1", "sd", "value"), rdpv(5, "Model 1", "sd", "value") / rdpv(5, "GDP(A)", "sd", "value"),
          rdpv(5, "Model 1", "rho1", "value"), NA, (rdpv(5, "Model 1", "sd", "value") / rdpv(5, "GDP(A)", "sd", "value"))^2)
rdpC <- c(rdpv(4, "Model 1", "w_E", "value"), rdpv(4, "Model 1", "w_I", "value"), rdpv(4, "Model 1", "w_P", "value"))
f2 <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "–", fmt(x, 2))
tr <- data.frame(
  Statistic = c("A. $\\rho$ (latent persistence)", "Latent innovation sd", "Error sd, E", "Error sd, I", "Error sd, P", "Long-run mean",
                "B. sd, GDP(A)", "sd, latent median path", "ratio of the two sds", "$\\rho_1$, latent median path",
                "variance ratio, per draw", "variance ratio, median path",
                "C. Closest combination: weight on E", "weight on I", "weight on P"),
  `RDP Model 1` = f2(c(rdpA, rdpB, rdpC)), check.names = FALSE)
for (cc in cols) tr[[cc[2]]] <- f2(c(colA(cc[1]), colB(cc[1]), colC(cc[1])))
tab(tr, align = paste0("l", strrep("r", ncol(tr) - 1)))
```

Four results stand out.

1. **On RDP 2014-12's sample, m2 reproduces their Model 1 closely.** Latent persistence is `r fmt(pv("m2_rdp", "rho"), 2)` against their `r fmt(rdpv(1, "Model 1", "rho"), 2)`. The latent innovation standard deviation is `r fmt(q(pv("m2_rdp", "tau")), 2)` against `r fmt(sqrt(rdpv(1, "Model 1", "sigma2_G")), 2)`. The error standard deviations are `r fmt(q(pv("m2_rdp", "sigma[1]")), 2)`, `r fmt(q(pv("m2_rdp", "sigma[2]")), 2)` and `r fmt(q(pv("m2_rdp", "sigma[3]")), 2)` (E, I, P) against `r fmt(sqrt(rdpv(1, "Model 1", "sigma2_E")), 2)`, `r fmt(sqrt(rdpv(1, "Model 1", "sigma2_I")), 2)` and `r fmt(sqrt(rdpv(1, "Model 1", "sigma2_P")), 2)`, with the same ordering: income noisiest, production cleanest. The posterior-median path has a standard deviation of `r fmt(r5("m2_rdp", "sd"), 2)` (RDP 2014-12: `r fmt(rdpv(5, "Model 1", "sd", "value"), 2)`) and first-order autocorrelation `r fmt(r5("m2_rdp", "rho1"), 2)` (`r fmt(rdpv(5, "Model 1", "rho1", "value"), 2)`). The weights of the closest fixed combination of E, I and P (their section 4.5.2) are `r fmt(r4("m2_rdp", "w_E"), 2)`, `r fmt(r4("m2_rdp", "w_I"), 2)` and `r fmt(r4("m2_rdp", "w_P"), 2)` against `r fmt(rdpv(4, "Model 1", "w_E", "value"), 2)`, `r fmt(rdpv(4, "Model 1", "w_I", "value"), 2)` and `r fmt(rdpv(4, "Model 1", "w_P", "value"), 2)`: somewhat more weight on production and less on expenditure. The largest gap is in the expenditure error, `r pc(q(pv("m2_rdp", "sigma[1]")) / sqrt(rdpv(1, "Model 1", "sigma2_E")) - 1)` larger in our fit. Different priors, a different sampler and thirteen years of data revisions otherwise change little. The published series over 1980–2013 also look the same on both vintages: the headline standard deviation is `r fmt(r5("headline", "sd"), 2)` on ours and `r fmt(rdpv(5, "GDP(A)", "sd", "value"), 2)` on theirs.
2. **The sample end changes the constant-variance model a great deal.** Fitted to 2026, m2 has persistence `r fmt(pv("m2_1980", "rho"), 2)` and a latent innovation standard deviation of `r fmt(q(pv("m2_1980", "tau")), 2)`, and its median path over 1980–2013 is less smooth (`r pc(sdr("m2_1980"))` of the headline standard deviation, against `r pc(sdr("m2_rdp"))` when fitted to 2013). `r if (any(P$key == "m2_e2019")) paste0("Fitted to 2019 Q4, m2 is close to the 2013 fit (persistence ", fmt(pv("m2_e2019", "rho"), 2), ", innovation sd ", fmt(q(pv("m2_e2019", "tau")), 2), ", path sd ", pc(sdr("m2_e2019")), " of the headline's). So the change comes from the COVID quarters, not from the 2013–19 data: a constant latent variance must accommodate a fall of ", fmt(-hl_2020q2 / 4, 1), " quarterly percentage points in 2020 Q2, which inflates the latent variance for every quarter and lowers persistence.") else ""`
3. **The latent-SV model is much less sensitive to the sample end.** m13's per-draw variance ratio over 1980–2013 is `r fmt(vr("m13_rdp", wR), 2)` when fitted to 2013 and `r fmt(vr("m13_prod", wR), 2)` when fitted to 2026; for m2 the two numbers are `r fmt(vr("m2_rdp", wR), 2)` and `r fmt(vr("m2_1980", wR), 2)`. m13's latent volatility can rise in 2020 without raising it in the 1990s.
4. **RDP 2014-12's headline result holds like-for-like, and the statistic matters.** Their posterior-median latent paths have standard deviations `r pc(1 - rdpv(5, "Model 1", "sd", "value") / rdpv(5, "GDP(A)", "sd", "value"))`, `r pc(1 - rdpv(5, "Model 2", "sd", "value") / rdpv(5, "GDP(A)", "sd", "value"))` and `r pc(1 - rdpv(5, "Model 3", "sd", "value") / rdpv(5, "GDP(A)", "sd", "value"))` below GDP(A)'s (Models 1–3). On the same sample and with the same statistic, our six models give `r pc(1 - max(sdr_rdp))` to `r pc(1 - min(sdr_rdp))` (@tbl-rdp-all). In variance terms the median paths have `r pc(min(sdr_rdp)^2)` to `r pc(max(sdr_rdp)^2)` of headline variance. The per-draw ratio of @sec-vardecomp is higher, `r pc(min(vr_rdp))` to `r pc(max(vr_rdp))`: a single plausible latent path is less smooth than the median path. By the per-draw measure, about `r pc(1 - max(vr_rdp))` to `r pc(1 - min(vr_rdp))` of measured variance over 1980–2013 is attributed to measurement error, against roughly half by the median-path measure.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-rdp-all
#| tbl-cap: "Six models fitted to 2013 Q2 (RDP 2014-12's sample end) and to 2026 Q2, all from 1980 Q1, statistics over 1980 Q1–2013 Q2. Variance ratio: per-draw var(μ)/var(headline), median and 90% interval. Path sd: sd of the posterior-median latent path relative to the sd of the headline."
ta <- data.frame(Model = m6,
  `Variance ratio, fit to 2013` = sapply(paste0(m6, "_rdp"), function(k) paste(fmt(vr(k, wR), 2), ci(vr(k, wR, "ratio_q05"), vr(k, wR, "ratio_q95"), 2))),
  `Variance ratio, fit to 2026` = sapply(m6, function(m) { k <- key80(m); paste(fmt(vr(k, wR), 2), ci(vr(k, wR, "ratio_q05"), vr(k, wR, "ratio_q95"), 2)) }),
  `Path sd, fit to 2013` = sapply(paste0(m6, "_rdp"), function(k) fmt(sdr(k), 2)),
  `Path sd, fit to 2026` = sapply(m6, function(m) fmt(sdr(key80(m)), 2)), check.names = FALSE)
tab(ta, align = "lrrrr")
```

@tbl-rdp-all shows the same comparison for all six models. On the RDP sample the models agree closely. On the longer sample they spread out. The constant-variance models m2 and m5 rise to `r fmt(vr("m2_1980", wR), 2)` and `r fmt(vr("m5_1980", wR), 2)`, because COVID inflates their constant latent variance. The measurement-SV models m4, m9 and m12 barely move over this window, although their 1980–2026 fits treat 2020 Q2 itself as measurement error (@sec-robust-sample). m13 moves much less than m2 and m5 (`r fmt(vr("m13_rdp", wR), 2)` to `r fmt(vr("m13_prod", wR), 2)`).

**What remains not comparable.** Estimating RDP 2014-12's Model 2 would need the latent–error correlations and the variance-ratio restriction, which none of our Stan programs has. Their Model 3 would need the unemployment rate. Their real-time results (Table 6) would need the 2001–2013 data vintages. None of these is in the repository.

# Limitations and further work {#sec-limits}

1. **Pseudo-real-time only.** Every forecast uses the 2026 Q2 vintage for all past quarters. The evaluation rewards models for predicting revised data, not first releases, and ignores revisions. RDP 2014-12 showed that their latent estimates were revised less than GDP(A) in real time [@rees2014, Table 6]; we cannot say whether ours are. Real-time scoring requires the ABS vintages and a refit per vintage.
2. **The production model is post hoc and its margin is thin.** m13 was proposed after the re-specified m10's results had been seen on the same evaluation window. Its margin over m12 is z = `r fmt(z13f, 2)` on the full sample and `r fmt(z138, 2)` on the 1980 sample. A two-try Bonferroni bar would not be met on either, and that bar understates the correction because at least four specifications in this line were scored on the same targets. The switch rule's extra condition (z ≥ 2 with first refit attempts only) guards against seed selection, not against specification search. The economic case for latent SV is strong (@fig-tau). The predictive case is suggestive.
3. **The evaluation window is reused.** All thirteen models, both samples and every round of the project use the same 146 targets. Re-scoring on the 1980 sample is not independent evidence. The cleanest test of the production model is its record on future ABS releases, scored as they arrive.
4. **The comparison does not test the variance decomposition.** Predictive scores evaluate forecasts of the observed measures. The split of measured growth into latent growth and error depends on the model's structure, and models that cannot be told apart by score can imply different splits (m7 and m1; @sec-vardecomp). The "about an eighth" (or "about a fifth excluding COVID") figure is a property of m13 on the 1980 sample.
5. **Labour signals.** Our fourth signal is hours worked, not RDP 2014-12's unemployment rate. No model combines m13's structure with a labour signal, so the value of labour data for the production model is unknown.
6. **Limited model checking.** Prior and posterior predictive checks were run only for the production model and its tighter-prior variant, and only after the comparison (@sec-ppc). The production priors are heavy-tailed. A variant with tighter priors, chosen from the prior predictive, changes little (@sec-robust-priors), but it still misses part of the plausibility target set for it, and it was not scored by LFO.
7. **Weak identification in places.** On the 1980 sample the persistence of expenditure-side volatility is close to its prior in m4, m9 and m12 and has a long tail in m13. m3's error correlations are weakly identified on both samples.
8. **One-step-ahead only.** We do not evaluate multi-step forecasts or the accuracy of the latent estimate itself (which is unobservable).
9. **Process.** Some diagnostics behind statements in this paper exist only in the project's research log, not as tables: the warmup-stall counts, the 1980-sample restart checks, and the old m10 mode table. Two long computing jobs stopped without an exit status and were resumed from checkpoints; resumed results were checked against re-created fits. The production fit's run time on GitHub's runners is known only from the repository README (about `r fact("ci_job_minutes")` minutes for the whole job).

Further work follows from the list: real-time scoring on ABS vintages; RDP 2014-12's Models 2 and 3; an m13 model with a labour signal; and scoring on future releases.

# Conclusion {#sec-conclusion}

We estimated thirteen state-space models of Australian GDP growth observed through the expenditure, income and production measures, and compared them by leave-future-out predictive density with latent states integrated out. Three conclusions are supported with different strength.

The strongest is that measurement errors are negatively serially correlated: a quarter's error is partly reversed the next quarter. The predictive gain holds on both samples and with or without stochastic volatility, and in the constant-variance comparison in every sub-period. It is consistent with the ABS reconciling the levels of the three measures annually.

The second is that the volatility of both measurement errors and true growth has changed a great deal. Measurement errors were much larger before 1980, and latent volatility fell from the 1980s to the 2010s before the COVID shock. Allowing measurement-error variance to change improves prediction, but about half the full-sample gain reflects the noisy pre-1980 data. Allowing latent variance to change gives the best model on every target, but by a thin, post hoc margin.

The third, and least tested, is the size of the measurement-error share. In the production model the variance of latent growth over 1980–2026 is `r pc(vr("m13_prod", "1980Q1-2026Q2"))` of headline variance; the COVID quarters, which the model assigns to true growth, raise that share. Over RDP 2014-12's window, 1980–2013, it is `r pc(vr("m13_prod", "1980Q1-2013Q2"))`. Re-estimated on their sample, our models put the latent share between `r pc(min(vr_rdp))` and `r pc(max(vr_rdp))`, and on their own statistic, the standard deviation of the median path, they reproduce their finding of a substantially smoother series. The predictive comparison does not discriminate between models that imply different shares. The most useful next step is real-time scoring on data vintages, which would also give an evaluation that does not reuse the window.

# Production-model history and switch rules {#sec-app-history}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-history
#| tbl-cap: "Production-model changes. Each model switch was decided by a rule fixed before the candidate's LFO results were known. All values are on the full sample unless stated. Times are local run times with four parallel chains on a six-core machine (m12: CmdStan sampling time; m13: wall time)."
g12ok <- all(G12$pass); g13ok <- all(G13f$pass); g138ok <- all(G138$pass)
hist <- data.frame(
  Change = c("m9 → m12 (2026-10-17)", "", "", "", "m12 → m13 (2026-10-18)", "", "", "", "", "Full sample → 1980 Q1 (2026-10-19)", "", ""),
  Condition = c("passes the gate on two seeds", "reliable LFO score (MCSE of difference)", "beats incumbent by z_NW ≥ 2", "local fit ≤ 30 min",
                "passes the gate on two seeds", "reliable LFO score (MCSE of difference)", "beats incumbent by z_NW ≥ 2", "z_NW ≥ 2 with first refit attempts only", "local fit ≤ 30 min",
                "no pre-set rule; owner's decision following RDP 2014-12's argument", "m13 passes the gate on two seeds (1980 sample)", "prediction: m13 from 1980 − m13 from 1959"),
  Observed = c(ifelse(g12ok, "yes (seeds 1, 2)", "no"), fmt(pw(PWf, "m12", "m9", "mcse_diff"), 2),
               paste0(sg(pw(PWf, "m12", "m9"), 2), " / ", fmt(pw(PWf, "m12", "m9", "se_diff_nw"), 2), " = ", fmt(pw(PWf, "m12", "m9", "z_nw"), 2)),
               paste0(fmt(fact("m12_prod_fit_secs") / 60, 0), " min"),
               ifelse(g13ok, "yes (seeds 1, 2)", "no"), fmt(pw(PWf, "m13", "m12", "mcse_diff"), 2),
               paste0(sg(pw(PWf, "m13", "m12"), 2), " / ", fmt(pw(PWf, "m13", "m12", "se_diff_nw"), 2), " = ", fmt(z13f, 2)),
               paste0(sg(rs(RSf, "m13", "m12", "first"), 2), " / ", fmt(rs(RSf, "m13", "m12", "first", "se_nw"), 2), " = ", fmt(rs(RSf, "m13", "m12", "first", "z_nw"), 2)),
               paste0(fmt(G13f$wall_secs[G13f$seed == 1][1] / 60, 1), " min (seed 1); ", fmt(G13f$wall_secs[G13f$seed == 2][1] / 60, 1), " min (seed 2, machine under load)"),
               "–", ifelse(g138ok, "yes (seeds 1, 2)", "no"),
               paste0(sg(FVSM$change[FVSM$model == "m13"], 2), ", NW z ", fmt(FVSM$change[FVSM$model == "m13"] / FVSM$se_nw_change[FVSM$model == "m13"], 2), " (below the z ≥ 2 bar)")))
tab(hist, align = "lll")
```

The production model was m9 (structural correlation and measurement SV) until 17 October 2026. It became m12 (adding AR(1) errors) and then, a day later, m13 (adding latent SV). Each switch rule was written down before the candidate's comparison results were known, and every model-switch condition in @tbl-history was met. The m12 → m13 rule added a fifth condition because m13 was a post-hoc candidate. The condition requires the z ≥ 2 margin to hold when every LFO refit uses its first sampling attempt, so that no retry with a new seed can create the margin. m13 needed no retry, so the condition changed nothing. The comparison author recommended treating m13 as a leading candidate rather than switching automatically, given the thin margin; the pre-set rule decided.

The move of the production sample to 1980 Q1 was not governed by a rule. The author of the comparison recommended keeping the full sample; the move was the project owner's decision, taken on RDP 2014-12's rationale. The prediction evidence was below the bar used for model switches, and the latent path barely moved. The decision rests on RDP 2014-12's argument that early measurement errors are unrepresentative, and on the evidence in @sec-robust-sample that pre-1980 data inflate the constant-variance models' error variances.

# Diagnostics {#sec-app-diag}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fitdiag
#| tbl-cap: "Full fits: 4 chains × (2000 warmup + 2000 draws), seed 1. div: divergent transitions of 8000; E-BFMI: minimum over chains; R-hat: maximum over hyperparameters; ESS: minimum bulk / tail over hyperparameters; s: sampling seconds. Full sample, then 1980 sample. m11's full-sample fit is not in the diagnostics table."
fdrow <- function(FD, s) data.frame(Sample = s, Model = FD$model, `adapt / depth` = paste0(FD$adapt_delta, " / ", FD$max_treedepth), div = FD$divergences,
  `E-BFMI` = fmt(FD$min_ebfmi, 3), `R-hat (var)` = paste0(fmt(FD$max_rhat_hyper, 4), " (", FD$worst_rhat_var, ")"),
  ESS = paste0(round(FD$min_ess_bulk_hyper), "/", round(FD$min_ess_tail_hyper)), `R-hat $\\mu$` = fmt(FD$max_rhat_mu, 4), `ESS $\\mu$` = round(FD$min_ess_bulk_mu),
  s = round(FD$wall_secs), check.names = FALSE)
tab(rbind(fdrow(FDf, "Full"), fdrow(FD8, "1980")), align = "llrrrrrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-gate
#| tbl-cap: "Production gate for m13, both samples and both seeds. Thresholds: divergences < 0.1%; min E-BFMI ≥ 0.3; R-hat ≤ 1.01 (hyperparameters), ≤ 1.05 ($\\mu_t$, $h_{t,k}$, $g_t$); bulk and tail ESS ≥ 400 (hyperparameters, $\\mu_t$)."
gt <- function(GT, s) {
  mets <- unique(sub(" \\(.*", "", GT$metric))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(1:2, function(sd) { x <- GT[GT$seed == sd, ]
    data.frame(Sample = s, Seed = sd, Metric = sub(" \\(.*", "", x$metric),
               Value = ifelse(grepl("divergences", x$metric), paste0(round(x$value * 8000), " of 8000"),
                              ifelse(grepl("ESS", x$metric), fmt(x$value, 0), fmt(x$value, 4))),
               Worst = x$worst, Pass = ifelse(x$pass, "yes", "no")) }))
}
gg <- rbind(gt(G13f, "Full"), gt(G138, "1980"))
gg$Value <- paste0(gg$Value, ifelse(gg$Worst != "", paste0(" (", gg$Worst, ")"), ""))
gg$key <- paste0(gg$Sample, ", seed ", gg$Seed)
wide <- reshape(gg[, c("Metric", "key", "Value")], idvar = "Metric", timevar = "key", direction = "wide")
names(wide) <- sub("^Value\\.", "", names(wide)); rownames(wide) <- NULL
tab(wide, align = "lrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lfodiag
#| tbl-cap: "LFO fits by model: number of stored fits, retried fits, failed attempts, fits with bulk ESS < 400 (weak mixing), and the worst diagnostics among stored fits. Full sample / 1980 sample."
lf <- function(m) {
  a <- LFDf[LFDf$model == m, ]; b <- LFD8[LFD8$model == m, ]
  data.frame(Model = m, Fits = paste(nrow(a), "/", nrow(b)), Retried = paste(mc(MCf, m, "n_fits_retried"), "/", mc(MC8, m, "n_fits_retried")),
             `Failed attempts` = paste(mc(MCf, m, "n_attempts_failed"), "/", mc(MC8, m, "n_attempts_failed")),
             `Weak mixing` = paste(sum(a$weak_mixing), "/", sum(b$weak_mixing)),
             `Max div` = paste(max(a$divergences), "/", max(b$divergences)),
             `Min E-BFMI` = paste(fmt(min(a$min_ebfmi), 2), "/", fmt(min(b$min_ebfmi), 2)),
             `Max R-hat` = paste(fmt(max(a$max_rhat), 3), "/", fmt(max(b$max_rhat), 3)),
             `Min bulk ESS` = paste(fmt(min(a$min_ess_bulk), 0), "/", fmt(min(b$min_ess_bulk), 0)), check.names = FALSE)
}
tab(do.call(rbind, lapply(paste0("m", 1:13), lf)), align = "lrrrrrrrr")
```

All stored LFO fits meet the refit rule (@tbl-lfodiag). On the full sample the weakest-mixing fits are those trained on data ending just after COVID, where the constant-latent-variance models' latent standard deviation mixes slowly. Weak mixing is not confined to those models: m13 has `r sum(LFDf$weak_mixing[LFDf$model == "m13"])` weak-mixing fits on the full sample and `r sum(LFD8$weak_mixing[LFD8$model == "m13"])` on the 1980 sample, all trained on data ending before 2020. On the 1980 sample the first attempt of m4's refit to 2016 Q2 failed badly (E-BFMI `r fmt(LRA8$min_ebfmi[LRA8$model == "m4" & !LRA8$kept], 3)`, R-hat `r fmt(LRA8$max_rhat[LRA8$model == "m4" & !LRA8$kept], 2)`); its second attempt passed. The diagnostics table records each fit's lowest bulk ESS but not the variable that has it.

# Filter tests {#sec-app-tests}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-tests
#| tbl-cap: "Unit tests of the filters (counts of passed expectations, from the test logs in output/sample_1980/logs/). All tests use the full-sample fits, except test_m13_tight.R, which uses the 1980-sample data."
tab(data.frame(`Test file` = paste0("tests/", TESTS$file), `Passed expectations` = TESTS$passed, `Failed blocks` = TESTS$failed_blocks, check.names = FALSE), align = "lrr")
```

Every filter used in estimation or evaluation is tested against a dense multivariate-normal computation (@tbl-tests; `r sum(TESTS$passed)` expectations in all, none failed). For m13 the tests check:

* the Stan Kalman filter's total and per-period log-likelihood against the dense multivariate-normal density of $y$ (to $10^{-9}$), for five settings of $\psi$ including $\psi = 0$, equal $\psi_E = \psi_I$ and $|\psi|$ up to 0.95, with non-constant $g$ and $h$, a jump of +5 in $g$, very small variances and extreme $z_{EI}$;
* bit-identity with m12's filter when $\tau_t$ is constant;
* FFBS draws against the dense smoother (20,000 draws; worst mean error about two Monte Carlo standard errors);
* the C++ filter used for LFO against the Stan filter (to $10^{-11}$) and against the fit's stored predictive log-likelihood on posterior draws;
* the particle filter against the exact Kalman filter as the volatilities of volatility go to zero, against m12's particle filter at $\omega_g = 0$, and against brute-force Monte Carlo over 200,000 simulated $(g, h)$ paths with a latent-volatility jump. The bootstrap and adapted proposals gave `r fact("pf_brute_force_boot")` and `r fact("pf_brute_force_adapt")` against a brute-force value of `r fact("pf_brute_force_ref")` (standard error 0.005).

Equivalent tests exist for m12, m3 and m10 and for the Kalman filters of the linear-Gaussian models. For the tighter-prior variant, `tests/test_m13_tight.R` checks that its filter code is byte-identical to m13's and returns identical output, and that at the same point (mapped between the two parameterisations) its log density differs from m13's only by the difference of the priors, on the 1980-sample data.

# Withdrawn results {#sec-app-withdrawn}

The project's record keeps superseded claims next to their corrections. The following were withdrawn and play no part in this paper.

* **PSIS-LOO rankings.** "m9 is best by LOO, `r fact("loo_old_m9_m4")` nats ahead of m4"; "SV gains about `r fact("loo_old_sv_gain")` nats"; an hours-model gain over m8 by LOO. These were invalid for the reasons in @sec-eval.
* **"Latent growth is 30–35% less variable than headline."** This was the variance of the posterior-mean path. The per-draw measure is in @sec-vardecomp.
* **The old m10's scores and variance ratio.** These came from a fit in mode A (@sec-failed); its particle-filter estimate for that mode did not converge in the particle count.
* **"m9 fixes m4's bimodal persistence."** The bimodality was a sampler artefact.
* **"The measurement-SV gain largely disappears from 1980."** This rested on two non-nested comparisons, m9 − m5 (`r sg(pw(PW8, "m9", "m5"))`, z `r fmt(pw(PW8, "m9", "m5", "z_nw"), 2)`) and m4 − m1 (`r sg(pw(PW8, "m4", "m1"))`, z `r fmt(pw(PW8, "m4", "m1", "z_nw"), 2)`). m9 drops the serial correlation that m5 has, and m4 adds a latent AR(1). The nested comparisons give the "roughly halves" result in @sec-comparison.
* **"m13 is the only three-measure model that keeps COVID in latent growth on both samples."** The constant-variance models also keep most of it there (@fig-covid).

# Reproduction {#sec-app-repro}

Every number in this paper is computed when the document is rendered, from four sources: `paper/data/*.csv`, `output/tables/*.csv`, `output/sample_1980/tables/*.csv` and `docs/*.json|csv`. The CSVs in `paper/data/` are extracted from the local fit objects by `paper/build_inputs.R`; no model is fitted there. Three of them are transcriptions rather than extractions, and say so: `rdp2014_reported.csv` (values published in RDP 2014-12), `record_facts.csv` (facts recorded only in the project's research log or Stan file headers, each with its source) and `test_counts.csv` (parsed from the test logs).

To rebuild from scratch:

1. `Rscript R/01_fetch_data.R` and `Rscript R/01b_fetch_research_data.R` (data; the ABS may have released a newer vintage).
2. The research suite on the full sample: `Rscript R/02_fit_models.R`, `Rscript R/fit_m11.R`, `Rscript R/fit_m12.R`, `Rscript R/fit_m13.R` (seeds 1 and 2, and `--omega_g_sd=1`), then `Rscript R/03_compare.R` (several hours).
3. The same on the 1980 sample, with `LATENTGDP_START=1980-03-01 LATENTGDP_OUT=output/sample_1980` (drivers in `output/sample_1980/`).
4. `Rscript R/fit_production.R` (the production fit).
5. The analyses added for this paper: `Rscript paper/fit_rdp_sample.R` (RDP-sample fits, output in `output/sample_rdp/`), `Rscript paper/fit_rdp_sample.R --end=2019-12-01 --out=output/sample_rdp/end2019 m2 m13` (fits ending in 2019 Q4), `LATENTGDP_START=1980-03-01 LATENTGDP_OUT=output/sample_1980 Rscript R/fit_m13.R --omega_g_sd=1 --out=output/sample_1980/fit_m13_omegag1.rds` (prior sensitivity on the production sample) and `Rscript paper/ppc_m13.R` (predictive checks). The driver `output/sample_rdp/run_new_analyses.sh` runs the fits in order. The tighter-prior variant: `Rscript paper/prior_candidates.R` (prior predictive choice), `bash output/sample_1980/run_tight.sh` (its fits on seeds 1 and 2 and on the RDP sample, through `R/fit_m13.R --variant=tight` and `paper/fit_rdp_sample.R m13_tight`), `Rscript tests/test_m13_tight.R` and `Rscript paper/ppc_m13.R --variant=tight`.
6. `Rscript paper/build_inputs.R` (about a minute), then `quarto render paper/latentgdp_wp.qmd`.

Steps 1–4 are documented in the repository's README. The fits are large (about 0.1–0.3 GB each) and are not committed; the tables and the CSVs in `paper/data/` are small and can be.
